clue.text: Aroused or bored to tears?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a deer or other animal in rut is sexually aroused, in the mating season
second meaning: stuck in a dull routine, tediously unvaried

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase serves two senses: the rutting season of stags, and the everyday idiom for a dreary routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The rut is the animal mating season, and the idiom for a monotonous routine uses the same three words.

clue.text: All agreed? In return, don't mention any of it

indicators.note: in return asks for the phrase built next to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: to name none, i.e. NAME NO: don't mention any
IT is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Someone asks if everyone is in agreement, and in exchange urges silence on the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME NO (don't mention any) plus SA (it, sex appeal) gives NAMENOSA, which read backwards becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in unanimous accord is acting as a single person, so everybody is in agreement.

clue.text: Heaven-sent female first to leave parade — appearing under the influence?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for parade departs

parts.note: a prom (promenade) is a seaside parade
on, as a performer appearing on stage is on
high, intoxicated by drink or drugs

explanation.surface: A woman leaves a parade early, seemingly drunk, as if a gift from the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: A PROM is a promenade, a parade along a seafront; losing its first letter P leaves ROM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent comes down from above, from God in the heights, which is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Limits opening move, sacrificing first piece

indicators.note: the chess image of giving up a piece: here the first letter is given up

parts.note: a gambit is a chess opening move

explanation.surface: A chess player's opening that sacrifices a pawn sets limits on the game.
explanation.walkthrough: A gambit is a chess opening in which a piece is sacrificed; here the clue sacrifices its first letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or extent of something, the bounds within which it operates.

clue.text: Charge wildly up to scree

indicators.note: wildly says the following letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber charges recklessly up a slope of loose scree.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute is to bring a legal charge against someone in court, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Load of articles in manuscript

indicators.note: in places the articles inside the abbreviation for manuscript

parts.note: A's: the indefinite article A, made plural with S

explanation.surface: A manuscript is stuffed full of articles.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles gives A plus S, the indefinite article in the plural, placed in MS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of something is a large quantity or heap, the same as a load of it.

clue.text: Ascribe onset of interference to Truss?

parts.note: to pin something on someone is to ascribe it to them

indicators.note: onset is the start, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: on, as in 'pin it to/on him'

explanation.surface: Blaming meddling on Liz Truss, the short-lived British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Truss looks like the former prime minister, but it is the verb meaning to tie up; the question mark flags the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinion someone is to bind their arms so they cannot move, which is trussing them up.

clue.text: Security association's billion put away, not whipped!

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations with its Security Council
to put away food is to eat it, so eaten

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a security body's billion has been stashed away but nobody got flogged.
explanation.definitionFit: A team not whipped or defeated in any match is undefeated, never beaten.

clue.text: Remedy problem with playing guitar?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quack medicine or pet cure
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words, NO STRUM, to see the guitarist's difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack cure or pet medicine, a supposed remedy for an ailment.

clue.text: In gear, learner's managed shift

indicators.note: managed in the sense of handled or worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver, in gear, manages to change gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' as in gear shift looks like part of the driving picture, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign something is to move or adjust it into a new position, so to shift it.

clue.text: Contact principal with singular sources of power

parts.note: to contact by phone is to ring
main means principal, chief
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with the chief, with a single power source in view.
explanation.walkthrough: A ring main is the circuit of household sockets in British wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring mains are the looped electrical circuits feeding household sockets, supplying electricity to appliances.

clue.text: Pronouncedly smooth-running train

indicators.note: pronouncedly means when said out loud, so the word is judged by sound

parts.note: an engine that runs smoothly is said to run sweet

explanation.surface: A railway train that runs remarkably smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: Train here is a retinue of attendants, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a retinue or body of attendants following a dignitary, which is a train.

clue.text: Misanthrope's harboured by antimonarchists

indicators.note: harboured by says the letters are sheltered within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A people-hater finds shelter among enemies of the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's man-hater.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens turns against all mankind after his friends abandon him, the classic hater of humanity.

clue.text: Muscle in with remodelling etc. in cupboard

indicators.note: in with tells us the muscle is placed inside the rest
remodelling means reshaping, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: AB is short for abdominal muscle

explanation.surface: Muscling in on remodelling a cupboard and its contents.
explanation.walkthrough: Muscle in looks like the idiom for intruding, but the abdominal muscle goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers for storing things.

clue.text: Poetical medium could be verbose, checking nothing and limp within

indicators.note: within says the limp word sits inside the remaining letters
could be suggests the word may be turned into another arrangement
checking as in stopping or holding back, so this letter is kept out

parts.note: O is the zero, nothing
lank hair is limp

explanation.surface: Wordy poetry, nothing to it and limp at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Checking means stopping, so the zero is kept out of the word; the limp word then sits right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blank verse is unrhymed iambic pentameter, the form of much of Shakespeare and Milton.

clue.text: One — Open All Hours, perhaps — homespun at heart, however it's made

parts.note: A means one
Open All Hours was a BBC situation comedy, an example of a sitcom

indicators.note: at heart takes the central pair of letters

explanation.surface: A homely TV comedy set in a corner shop that is homespun at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: Open All Hours was a British sitcom about a corner shop; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something as it comes means accepting it in whatever form it arrives, without choosing.

clue.text: Consecutive results gaining position where success is guaranteed

parts.note: two wins in a row
a situation is a position or job

explanation.surface: Two good results in a row secure a place where victory is certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A win-win situation is a state of affairs in which every party gains, so nobody can lose.

clue.text: Harry follows Hunter, say, as monitor

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so this word goes second

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover
to harry someone is to dog or hound them

explanation.surface: Harry trails a hunter as a lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name and Hunter a person; harry is the verb to pester, and a hunter is a pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a body that oversees and monitors conduct, keeping guard over others.

clue.text: A's appetite?

parts.note: A is the letter at the centre of the word MAN, its inner part

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about whose appetite this is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as wordplay describes the clue: A is the middle letter of MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is a jocular expression for the stomach and its hunger, as in feeding it.

clue.text: Initial strike has waterway seething

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
seething means boiling, so hot

explanation.surface: A first blow lands while a river boils.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's tee shot is the first stroke played on each hole.

clue.text: Kiev I'd nearly upended carrying salad

indicators.note: upended says the hidden letters are read backwards
carrying says the words hold the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chicken Kiev almost toppled over the side salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'carrying salad' as the definition, but 'carrying' is the signal that the words hold the letters, so only 'salad' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory plant eaten raw as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: Quite nauseated (in front and back) sitting in car

indicators.note: sitting in places the picked letters inside the car's name

parts.note: Kia is a car maker

indicators.note: front and back takes the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Somewhat sick, sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Kia is a Korean car brand; N and D, the ends of nauseated, sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinda is a casual spelling of 'kind of', meaning somewhat or rather.

clue.text: Son casually blind to tears in new costume

indicators.note: blind to means ignoring the letters, and casually says they are scattered, not together
new suggests the remaining letters are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A son is carelessly oblivious to the rips in a new outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, O and N from TO TEARS IN, leaving TTEARI, and rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is clothing, dress or outfit, so it can stand for a costume.

clue.text: Exercise — good for wind, possibly?

parts.note: a musical study written as practice, which might suit wind instruments, not the lungs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests physical exercise for the breath; it is a practice piece of music that might be scored for wind players.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a musical study, a piece composed to practise technique on an instrument.

clue.text: It's hell in headdress — regularly removed

indicators.note: every other letter is taken out at regular intervals, keeping the odd ones

explanation.surface: Wearing a headdress is torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek underworld, often used to mean the infernal place of punishment.

clue.text: Old-fashioned divine last seen in Christmas BBC murder mystery

indicators.note: last seen in takes the final letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A festive BBC whodunnit's final sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Divine is a verb here, not a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To scry is an archaic word for foretelling the future by crystal gazing, i.e. to prophesy.

clue.text: Constantly busy — doing dressage, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rushing about with no rest
second meaning: a horse moving at a trot, as in dressage

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being run off one's feet is taken literally as a horse trotting.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means continuously active, and literally describes a horse moving at a trotting gait.

clue.text: Heads back to clubhouse after getting bowled within a few deliveries

indicators.note: after places the clubhouse letter at the end
within puts the bowled letter inside the deliveries

parts.note: in cricket an over is six deliveries, so overs
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: back to takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled out within a few balls heads back to the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: Heads looks like a verb (goes back) but is the noun, the face side of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin is the side bearing the head, so it is heads, not tails.

clue.text: Lose heart when one article ignored Paradise Lost

indicators.note: ignored means the article is left out of the letters
lost means the letters wander from their place into a new order

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone gives up after skipping one article on Milton's epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Paradise Lost is Milton's poem, but 'Lost' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up hope, so lose heart is a straight synonym.
